part2.intro: Three young people talk about their hobbies.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Phong
texts.text: I collect old cameras. I've got thirty-two now! My grandpa gave me the first one for my ninth birthday – it was his camera when he was young. I find most of them at markets, and they're usually quite cheap. Some of them still work, and I take black and white photographs with them. My friends think it's a strange hobby, but my photos always look different from theirs.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Ruby
texts.text: Every Saturday I go to a drawing club at the art museum in the city. There are about fifteen members, and most of them are adults. We draw the paintings and other things in the museum. I've learned a lot from the older members. Next month the museum is going to put some of our drawings on the wall for visitors – I'm so excited! I want to study art at university.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Kofi
texts.text: I play the guitar in a band with my cousin and two friends from school. We practise in my cousin's garage every Sunday afternoon. Our neighbours sometimes get angry because we're too loud! Last summer we played at a music festival in our town – it was our first time on a stage. I was really nervous, but it went well. I'd love to be a musician one day.

part3.title: The boy who gives away bikes
part3.text:
When Sam Okoro was twelve, someone stole his bike from outside the library. "I was really upset," he says. "My parents didn't have enough money for a new one, so my uncle helped me to build one from old parts."

Sam enjoyed it so much that it became his hobby. Now fifteen, he spends most weekends in his uncle's garage, repairing old bikes that people don't want any more. "People give them to us. Some of them are in a terrible state – last month someone brought one with no wheels!"

But Sam doesn't keep the bikes. He gives them to children in his town whose families don't have much money. So far, he has given away forty-three bikes. "The best part is seeing the children's faces when they ride for the first time," he says.

Sam's hobby takes a lot of time. "I used to play football on Saturdays, but I stopped because I didn't have time for both. I don't miss it, though." His school friends sometimes help him, and last year he started a bike club at school. The club now has twenty members, and they meet every Wednesday after school.

This summer, Sam and the club members are going on a cycling holiday together. They are going to ride to the beach, a hundred kilometres away, and stay at a campsite for three nights. "We'll take tents and cook our own food," says Sam. "I can't wait!"

part4.title: The first cameras
part4.text:
Today almost everyone can take photographs with their phone, but two hundred years ago it was very different. The oldest photograph in the world was {19} in France in 1826 or 1827. It shows the view from a window, and the camera needed eight hours to make the picture!

Later, cameras became faster, but people still had to sit without {20} for several minutes. Cameras were also very expensive, so many people only had their photograph taken once or twice in their {21}.

In 1888, an American company sold the first camera that was easy to use. It was small and light, and anyone could {22} it. When you finished your film, you {23} the whole camera back to the company, and they printed your photographs.

Photography soon became a popular hobby. Today, millions of people around the world are {24} of photography clubs, and some of them still prefer to use old cameras with film.

items.q: What is the girl's new hobby?

script.t: Are you still going to dance classes, Rosie?
No, I stopped in the summer. I've started a new hobby now.
Is it photography? I saw you with a camera yesterday.
That was my brother's camera. No, I've started painting. I go to a class at the museum on Saturday mornings.

items.q: What will the boys do on Saturday?

script.t: Do you want to go for a bike ride on Saturday, Josh?
I can't. My bike's broken, and Dad can't repair it until next week.
Oh. What about a picnic in the park, then?
It's going to rain all weekend. Let's do something inside.
OK, let's go to the new science museum. It's free on Saturdays.
Great idea!

items.q: How much did the girl pay for her concert ticket?

script.t: Are you going to the concert on Friday? How much was your ticket?
Normal tickets are twenty-four pounds.
Twenty-four! I only paid twelve pounds last year.
Everything's more expensive now. But I'm a member of the band's fan club, so I only paid twenty.
That's not bad. Are you going with Lucy?
Yes, her mum's going to drive us there.

items.q: What does the boy collect?

script.t: What's in all these boxes, Jamie? Are they your grandad's stamps?
Yes, he collected stamps for fifty years. But I don't – I think they're boring.
What do you collect, then? Coins?
I tried collecting coins, but it was too expensive. I collect football cards. I've got nearly five hundred now!

items.q: Where is the girl's guitar?

script.t: Dad, have you seen my guitar? I've got a lesson in half an hour.
Isn't it under your bed? That's where you usually keep it.
No, I've looked there.
Did you leave it at school after the concert?
No, you drove me home after the concert, remember? I had it with me.
Oh dear, it's still in the car! I forgot to bring it in. Sorry!

part2.intro: You will hear a man talking about a photography competition for young people.
part2.title: Young Photographers Competition

items.label: Number of photos you can send:
Last day to send photos: June

script.t: Hello, I'm Paul from the Westbridge Photography Club, and I'm here to tell you about our competition for young photographers. Anyone aged eleven to sixteen can enter. Last year the subject was people, and we got some wonderful photos of families and friends. This year the subject is animals. Your photos can show pets, farm animals or wild animals – it's up to you. You can send us three photos, but please don't send more than that! The last day to send your photos is the fourteenth of June. The winner will get a fantastic prize. Last year it was a computer, but this year it's a new camera from the camera shop on King Street. There are also prizes for second and third place – books about photography. The best photos will be in the town museum during the summer holidays. Our judge this year is a famous photographer, Mr Dawson. That's D-A-W-S-O-N. He has taken photos of animals for lots of magazines. To find out more, come to one of our club meetings on Thursday evenings.

part3.intro: You will hear Ben talking to his friend Chloe about a quiz club.

items.q: Why did Ben join the quiz club?
options: He likes going to the library.

items.q: Which questions are the most difficult for Ben?
Where will the big quiz be?
What happened in the competition last year?
What will Chloe do at the competition?

script.t: Hi Ben. Did I see you in the library at lunchtime? You never go there!
Ha! I've joined the quiz club. We meet there on Mondays and Wednesdays.
The quiz club? Why? Did Mr Hill ask you to join?
He asked everyone in our class, but that's not the reason. My cousin Leo is the captain, and he said they needed someone who knows a lot about sport. So I said yes.
Well, you do know everything about football! What do you do at the club?
We practise with old quiz questions. There are questions about history, science, music... History's OK, but music is the hardest for me. I only know the bands my sister listens to!
And is there a competition?
Yes, there's a big quiz for schools in March. It's at the city museum. The winners get books for their school library and a trip to London.
Wow. Do you think you'll win?
Probably not! Last year our team came fourth. But the other members are really clever, so we might.
Can people come and watch?
Yes, family and friends can come, and it's free. Why don't you come? You could bring your camera and take photos of our team for the school magazine.
Great idea! I need some photos for my next article anyway.

script.t: My grandpa gave me his old MP3 player last month. It isn't small – it's quite big, actually – and it was expensive when he bought it. But it's got about two thousand songs on it from the sixties and seventies. I listen to it every day on the bus, and I've found lots of great bands that I didn't know before!

script.t: How was the toy museum, Ella?
I thought it would be boring – it's just old toys, right? But actually it was brilliant. You can play with lots of the toys, and there's a room where you can make your own.
Was it crowded?
No, it wasn't busy at all. You should go!

Tim's guitar teacher, Anna, is playing in a concert on Thursday evening, so she can't teach him at six o'clock this week. Could Tim come at four o'clock instead, on the same day? The price is the same, of course. Please call me back. Thanks.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking about her hobby.
items.q: How does the girl feel about her hobby now?

script.t: I started drawing comics two years ago. At first they weren't very good, and I was worried that people would laugh at them. But I practised every day, and last month the school magazine printed one of my stories. Everyone in my class read it! My mum put a copy on the fridge, and I smile every time I see it.

part5.intro: You will hear Nina talking to her uncle about her new friends. What is each friend's hobby?

script.t: So, Nina, how's your new school? Have you made any friends?
Yes, lots! There's Alex. He sits next to me in maths. He's always drawing in his book, but his real hobby is the guitar. He practises every evening and he wants to start a band.
Great! Who else?
Hana. She used to go to dance classes, but she stopped last year. Now she's crazy about photography. She takes her camera everywhere.
And the boy you talked about yesterday? Ryan?
Ryan collects old coins. He's got coins from more than forty countries! His brother loves reading, but Ryan says books are boring.
Ha! And Sophie? Does she like taking photos too?
No, Sophie's a dancer. She goes to classes four times a week, and she's in a show at the theatre next month. Her family goes camping every summer, but she doesn't really like it.
And does anyone like art, like you?
Yes, Minh. He draws amazing pictures of animals. He wants to make films one day, but at the moment he just draws all the time.
They all sound really nice.
